summary: A large open-air night market behind Seacon Square, known for its vintage and second-hand stalls alongside food, drinks and live-music bars. It is an east-Bangkok outing with a local feel and enough space to browse for hours; travel there from central Bangkok takes planning.
whyGo: Browse vintage clothing, second-hand objects, antiques and collectibles in a sprawling market setting.
Make an evening of street food, casual drinks and live music, with several distinct areas to explore.
Pair the market with Seacon Square or nearby attractions in eastern Bangkok.
bestFor: Vintage and second-hand shoppers who enjoy unplanned browsing
Travellers looking for an evening of food, shopping and drinks
Visitors with a Thursday-to-Sunday night free and comfortable with a longer cross-city trip
skipIf: You have little time and want a night market near central Bangkok
You dislike crowds, outdoor heat, or large areas with lots of walking
You need confirmed step-free routes or accessible facilities throughout the site
duration: Allow 2–3 hours as a planning estimate for a wander and meal; the venue is large, and Trip.com suggests 3–5 hours for sightseeing.
cost: Entry is listed as free by Trip.com. Food, drinks, shopping and transport are extra; no reliable current stall price list was found. Bring Thai baht cash and ask about prices and payment methods at individual stalls.
hours: The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists Thursday–Sunday, 17:00–24:00. Dusit Princess Srinakarin lists Thursday–Sunday, 17:00–01:00, so closing time is inconsistent; check the market’s official Facebook page or call +66 81 827 5885 before a late visit.
bestTime: Go on a Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday evening. Arriving after 19:00 is suggested by the hotel’s visitor guide, though it may be busier then; arrive earlier if you want to browse before eating.
gettingThere: The market is behind Seacon Square on Srinagarindra Road, Prawet. The Tourism Authority of Thailand says Suan Luang Rama IX Yellow Line station is about a 10-minute walk away. MRTA confirms a connecting walkway between that station (YL15) and Seacon Square; follow local signs from the mall toward the market. A taxi or ride-hail can simplify the last leg. From central Bangkok, allow extra time for the cross-city journey and verify the return route and train hours.
booking: No booking is listed for general market entry; go directly and pay individual vendors. Special events or performances may have separate arrangements, which were not verified.
accessibility: The sources reviewed do not document step-free access through the market, accessible toilets or seating. Expect extensive walking through open-air lanes that may be crowded or uneven; contact the venue ahead if you need specific access information.
practicalTips: Check the market’s Facebook page on the day: published closing times differ, and holiday schedules may change.
Wear comfortable shoes and carry water; the market covers a large area and is mostly outdoors.
Bring small cash notes, compare prices, and ask clearly before purchasing second-hand goods.
Keep valuables secure in busy lanes and agree on a fare or use a metered/ride-hail taxi for the return trip.
decemberNotes: A December 2026 visit should fit a Bangkok evening if it falls Thursday–Sunday. No 2026 holiday hours or December event programme was verified. Confirm the open day, closing time and transport home close to the date; the market is far from central Bangkok.
uncertainties: Published closing time differs: the Tourism Authority of Thailand says midnight, while the hotel guide says 01:00.
Current vendor prices, card acceptance, accessible facilities and any December 2026 special hours remain unverified.
